explanation: Renaissance Italian writers such as Giorgio Vasari used the label to sneer at the style as barbaric, as if the Goths who sacked Rome had built it. Its builders simply called it French work.

claims.text: The term Gothic for medieval architecture was first used by Renaissance Italian writers as a disparaging label.
Giorgio Vasari used the label 'Gothic' disparagingly, associating the style with the barbarian Goths.
In the Middle Ages the style was known as opus francigenum, French work.
